claims.statement: For the CB matching sector obtained by stripping its fixed root and arm leaf, the colored quotient-ring theorem applies exactly to the ordinary lower shadow: Chong Theorems 1.2(i) and 2.1(iii) imply revlex shadow minimization for the matching-sector face poset. This theorem and its associated unweighted normalized-matching flow do not imply preservation or control of the additional hub-insertion boundary. A three-vertex colored graph gives an exact obstruction to automatic preservation of an endpoint-sensitive insertion count under revlex compression.
claims.scope: The matching-sector ordinary shadow and the general failure of an unweighted compression argument to preserve an endpoint-sensitive extra insertion count. The small obstruction is not a CB-tree counterexample and does not decide the full mixed inequality or the primary aggregate.
claims.reason: The quotient-ring/type bridge and its ordinary-shadow consequence are exact. The toy graph calculation is exact and shows the auxiliary count can change under compression. No argument transports all CB hub-insertion arcs for arbitrary source subsets, and no complete CB mixed-boundary cut or counterexample was established.

limitations: The CB direction note supplies a sector description but no complete CB edge encoding for this route, so the toy graph is only a compression obstruction model and not a CB witness.

The literature results control ordinary unweighted shadows or adjacent-rank matching flow; they do not include the selected-tag mixed boundary, competing hub-target demand, or the complete tree aggregate.
No universal theorem, counterexample, full selector audit, or weighted-Hall certificate was established.
